newsitem.title: INDIA: India IPCL sets 60-bln rupee investments.
newsitem.headline: India IPCL sets 60-bln rupee investments.

text.p: The state-run Indian Petro-Chemicals Corportion Limited (IPCL) will invest 60 billion rupees in the government's Ninth Five-Year Plan (1997-2002), the government said on Monday.

The statement quoted Chemicals and Fertilizers Minister Shees Ram Ola as telling a parliamentary committee that the company's investment would include an expansion of existing facilities and setting up of new projects.

"This includes a 9.0-billion rupee project involving expansion of of LLDPE/HDPE production capacity and enhancement of ethylene production capacity from 400,000 tonnes per annum (tpa) to 500,000 tonnes per annum," the statement said.
"A new project with 160,000 tpa of LDPE capacity along with 300,000 tpa of ethylene production capacity will be set up at Vadodara (Baroda) at a cost of 20 billion rupees," the statement said.
It added that a new ACN (acrylonitrile) installation has been planned at Gandhar with a capacity of 100,000 tpa at a cost of 14.0 billion rupees.
IPCL will also build a composite refinery and plans to set up facilities to produce acrylic fibre, yarn and power at a total cost of about 12.0 billion rupees, the statement said.
"With this investment, IPCL is set to become the largest manufacture of ethylene in India," it said.
IPCL planned to fund 60 percent of its investments with internal resources and raise debt for the remaining 40 percent, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
